# Support matrix

<!-- This file is generated by `just capability-docs-write`. Do not edit it manually. -->

This matrix is generated from the machine-readable `CAPABILITY_LEDGER` in
`libarchive_oxide-core`. A format or method is supported only in the directions shown;
an empty direction is a recognized, structured `Unsupported` path rather than a claim of
implementation. Cargo requirements must also be enabled in the consuming build.

## Archive formats

| Format | Read access | Write access | Portable | Native | Requirements | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tar | sequential | sequential | read/write | read/write | — | v7, ustar, pax, and GNU dialects; archive and entry metadata are lossless-or-error, preserving exact 12-bit permission modes, opaque global PAX and last-wins comment multiplicity alongside coherent typed entry comments/owners/times/xattrs/ACL fields, field-exact GNU sparse records, and Char/Block devices through the 8-byte base-256 maximum; global keys that override future entries, foreign extensions, typed/raw conflicts, higher mode bits, untyped or unsupported sparse/device properties, and unsupported filesystem fields or kinds fail before entry output |
| cpio | sequential | sequential | read/write | read/write | — | binary LE/BE, odc, newc, and crc; 12-bit permission modes, owner IDs, non-negative whole-second mtime, dialect-bounded inode/link/device/size fields, and dialect-correct CRC sums are lossless-or-error, with required-size, reserved TRAILER!!! path, and default-newc u32 projection shared by transcoding; higher mode bits and unsupported or lossy entry fields are rejected before output |
| ar | sequential | sequential | read/write | read/write | — | GNU, BSD, and thin-member metadata; control-looking short paths plus long paths use four-byte-padded BSD inline names, while 12-bit regular-file mode, fixed-width numeric owner, non-negative whole-second mtime, and ten-digit member size including padded inline-name bytes are lossless-or-error; missing sizes, higher mode bits, unsupported kinds, lossy times, and numeric overflow are rejected before output |
| zip | sequential | sequential | read/write | read/write | — | bounded forward-only local-header reads for Store/Deflate/Deflate64/BZip2/LZMA/Zstandard/XZ/PPMd8, including signed classic/ZIP64 descriptors and unsigned descriptors for self-terminating Deflate/Deflate64/BZip2/PPMd8, EOS-terminated LZMA, and a single standard Zstandard frame; LZMA and PPMd8 use acknowledged pull-worker input so only range-decoder-owned bytes are committed. ZipCrypto and WinZip AES Store/Deflate/BZip2/LZMA/Zstandard/XZ/PPMd8 use the same path with ordered OpenOptions password candidates; EOS-terminated LZMA, PPMd8, and Deflate64 additionally compose with both wrappers under known sizes or signed/unsigned classic/ZIP64 descriptors. Seek reads retain every listed method and encryption profile and project non-directory central-directory DOS attributes into typed file flags. Standard multi-disk archives use caller-owned bounded VolumeSet sources or explicit terminal .zip/.z01 path discovery, translate classic and ZIP64 disk-relative central/local offsets, and compose with every supported compression/encryption decoder; nonempty archive/file comments, exact typed owner/time/12-bit permission-mode/low-byte non-directory DOS file-flag fields, field-coherent timestamp/Unix-owner and applicable Unicode path/comment extras, non-structural two-byte raw extras, serialized pathname bounds, and bounded metadata-owned unencrypted symlink targets are lossless-or-error; higher mode or file-flag bits, indistinguishable empty typed comments, unsupported kinds/fields, typed/raw conflicts, encrypted symlinks, and container-owned or malformed extras are rejected or reported by transcoding |
| 7z | seek | seek | read/write | read/write | `sevenz` | general coder-graph reader with bounded caller-owned split-volume input and explicit path-based numeric sibling discovery; solid and one-folder-per-stream writers across every listed coder; File/Dir/Symlink path/mode/size/target metadata, non-structural Windows file flags, and checked full-range u64 FILETIME mtimes are lossless-or-error, metadata-owned symlink payloads transcode without duplication, unknown archive/file properties round-trip, and unrepresentable typed fields plus end-marker or container-owned raw properties fail before entry output; archive metadata replacement accounts only the current bounded property set |
| iso9660 | seek | seek | read/write | read/write | — | ISO 9660, Rock Ridge/SUSP continuation areas, Joliet, and bounded multi-extent/interleaved/extended-attribute reads with typed ECMA owner, permission, and year 0–9999 time metadata at exact 10 ms precision; writes and transcoding preserve File/Dir/Symlink/Char/Block/Fifo/Socket kinds, u32-bounded PX/PN owner/inode/link/device metadata, 12-bit modes, and u32 entry sizes, while hardlinks, owner names, comments, required out-of-range devices, and other unrepresentable typed fields fail before output or become explicit optional-field losses; primary/Joliet descriptor geometry, declared volume bounds, and per-record volume-sequence checks prevent mis-sized, trailer, or cross-volume reads; PVD-exact volume names, nonempty/non-trimmed system/application identifiers, and canonical unknown SUSP fields round-trip losslessly, and replacement accounts only the current metadata |
| udf | seek | — | read | read | — | read-only UDF 1.02–2.60 with Metadata, Sparable, Metadata-over-Sparable, and Virtual/VAT Partition translation, short/long/extended allocation descriptors, streams, and external EA spaces; writer is intentionally absent |
| cab | seek | — | read | read | — | read-only; explicit bounded multi-cabinet continuation through root VolumeArchiveReader over OpenOptions and caller-owned VolumeSet |
| xar | seek | seek | read/write | read/write | — | Store/zlib/BZip2 seek writer with independent per-entry streams, codec-memory preflight, encoded-expansion bounds, and a bounded spill-to-disk heap spool |
| empty | sequential | — | read | read | — | canonical zero-byte archive; read-only |
| raw | sequential | — | read | read | — | explicit single-entry byte stream; never auto-detected; read-only |
| warc | sequential | sequential | read/write | read/write | — | WARC 1.0 and 1.1 records; strict bounded CRLF framing, required declared content sizes, streamed content blocks, and lossless named-field extensions; virtual entry paths are collision-free record-ID/sequence projections and mode is normalized to 0644, both reported explicitly by transcoding |
| rar-legacy | sequential | — | read | read | — | bounded RAR 3.x/4.x container, Store entries, and feature-gated clean-room RAR3 LZ77/Huffman plus PPMd-H/PPMd-II blocks for methods 0x31-0x35 with decoded CRC32; AES-gated RAR3 AES-128-CBC reads decrypt bounded headers and non-solid, non-split file data through ordered OpenOptions candidates, cache zeroizing candidate keys per salt, and release plaintext only after exact size and CRC32 validation; all five standard RAR3 VM filters use validated fingerprints and closed-enum execution without arbitrary bytecode interpretation; one concrete decoder retains either LZ dictionary/Huffman/distance state or the bounded PPMd model plus its shared output window and standard-program table across sequential solid members; packed, unpacked, ciphertext/candidate/output, fixed workspace, filter programs/queue/scratch, and requested PPMd heap bytes are preflighted against in-flight and codec-memory budgets, including one retained packed copy for bounded non-solid split-volume joins; arbitrary VM programs and encrypted solid, split-volume, or symlink payloads remain typed unsupported; checksum-verified streamed auxiliary/recovery blocks are reported without repair; raw flags, Unicode names, times, ownership/modes/attributes, SFX, 64-bit sizes, Store symlinks, bounded VolumeSet Store/compressed joins, and adjacent-volume discovery are preserved; writing is license-excluded |
| rar5 | sequential | — | read | read | — | bounded RAR5 container, Store entries, and feature-gated clean-room generation-0 RAR5 LZ77/Huffman methods 1-5 with x86 E8/E9, Delta, and ARM filters plus decoded CRC32/BLAKE2sp verification; AES-gated RAR5 AES-256-CBC reads decrypt bounded headers, services, and single-volume non-solid Store/LZ file data through at most 16 ordered OpenOptions password candidates, a finite PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 budget, zeroizing cached keys, bounded AES-padding replay, and raw or HMAC-tweaked CRC32/BLAKE2sp authentication before plaintext release; exact dictionaries, each self-described encoded block, ciphertext/candidate/output, filter scratch, and the pending-filter queue are preflighted against codec-memory and in-flight budgets without bounding total packed size; one bounded concrete decoder state continues unencrypted generation-0 compressed file members across both sequential solid and caller-owned VolumeSet boundaries with per-part and logical checksums, while independently compressed comment/quick-open/recovery/ACL/alternate-stream services use a separate concrete decoder and decoded-size budgets without leaking service bytes as entry data; CRC-checked unknown headers carrying skip-if-unknown discard their exact data extent without allocation; generation 1/RAR7, encrypted solid/split members, encrypted payloads without CRC32/BLAKE2sp, solid or split services, and rare filter types 4-7 remain typed unsupported; comments, quick-open/recovery reporting without repair, ACL/alternate-stream records, names/times/ownership/attributes/versions/links/extras, adjacent-volume discovery, and Store joins are preserved; writing is license-excluded |
| lha | seek | — | read | read | `lha` | read-only levels 0–3; bounded lh0/lh1/lh2/lh3/lh4/lh5/lh6/lh7/lhx/lzs/lz4/lz5/pm0/pm1/pm2 payloads with CRC16 verification; lh2/lh3 preflight whole packed/output buffering while the other compressed methods stream fixed dictionaries; MZ SFX prefixes are scanned with a fixed 4 KiB window through 20 KiB and their byte length is reported |
| mtree | sequential | sequential | read/write | read/write | — | mtree v1/v2 manifests; octal escapes including comment-looking names, defaults, relative NUL-free traversal, typed metadata, and unknown keyword preservation; unrepresentable paths fail before output, and contents paths are metadata only and never opened |

## Outer compression filters

| Filter | Read access | Write access | Portable | Native | Requirements | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gzip | filter | filter | read/write | read/write | — | — |
| compress | filter | filter | read/write | — | `compress` | Unix compress(1) .Z stream using bounded portable LZW read/write |
| lzip | filter | filter | read/write | — | `lzip` | strict concatenated lzip reads and canonical single-member writes with bounded LZMA dictionaries |
| bzip2 | filter | filter | read/write | read/write | `bzip2` | — |
| zstd | filter | filter | read/write | read/write | `zstd` | — |
| xz | filter | filter | read/write | read/write | `xz` | — |
| lz4 | filter | filter | read/write | read/write | `lz4` | — |
| deflate | filter | — | read | read | `sevenz` | raw RFC 1951 stream; structurally selected by 7z and never auto-probed |
| lzma-alone | filter | filter | read/write | — | `lzma` | bounded portable LZMA1 read/write; explicit-only because the 13-byte header has no magic |
| lzop | filter | filter | read/write | — | `lzop` | bounded concatenated-member read with Safe Rust LZO1X decompression and deterministic stored-block write |
| uuencode | filter | filter | read/write | read/write | — | bounded POSIX framing; compatible space/backtick decoding and canonical 45-byte-line writing |
| base64 | filter | filter | read/write | read/write | — | strict RFC 4648 Base64 with canonical padding; explicit-only to avoid text false positives |
| rpm | filter | — | read | read | — | bounded RPM lead/header removal; emits the payload for nested compression and cpio detection |

Direction values are `read`, `write`, `read/write`, or `—`. The portable and native
columns describe backend capability, not which Cargo features happen to be enabled in one
particular binary. Use `oxarchive capabilities --json` for build-specific `available`,
`disabled`, and `unsupported` states.
